subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: How should plain provider text such as `LLM error api_error: Internal server error` be classified for cron/fallback, and should that class affect shared auth-profile cooldown?
rationale: Current code has separate semantics for `timeout`, `overloaded`, and `server_error`, and choosing the wrong class can either poison shared provider health, skip useful fallback, or leave cron jobs waiting for the watchdog.

options.title: Use cron-local server_error
options.body: Classify the plain SDK shape as a retryable `server_error` for cron/fallback while keeping shared auth-profile cooldown behavior local unless maintainers explicitly widen it.

options.title: Treat as overloaded cooldown
options.body: Classify plain API internal-server errors as `overloaded` so same-provider profiles cool down and cross-provider fallback is favored, accepting broader provider-health side effects.

options.title: Keep timeout semantics
options.body: Leave generic internal-server text as `timeout` and document that cron retry/backoff or stream-stall work, not failover classification, owns this recovery path.

recommendation.title: Use cron-local server_error
recommendation.body: Classify the plain SDK shape as a retryable `server_error` for cron/fallback while keeping shared auth-profile cooldown behavior local unless maintainers explicitly widen it.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the overlapping structured `server_error` cron retry fix and have adjacent failover classification history.
